answer: Agents can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed if it repeatedly makes claims contradicted by later evidence. A reputation-weighted, randomly sampled jury checks disputes, while one bond covers only one active identity at a time; splitting influence across a dune of accounts therefore requires locking more capital and risks more collateral being burned. A garden of cheap accounts gains no extra weight unless each is funded, and the delta between attack cost and expected reward can make Sybil control uneconomic.
